body:
#2008 (BUG-1303) REVIEWED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED — the drain is at phase 2 on that spec right now, so the PR belongs to the live drive and its reviewer has not run. I merged over a live drive an hour ago and am not repeating it the same night.

That is also the first use of the rule I wrote after that breach: read the drain's CURRENT SPEC and compare it to the PR's spec, rather than reading a phase list and inferring. It took one command and it changed what I did.

THE WIDENED CRITERIA ARE HONOURED. No cfg gate anywhere, which matters because a platform-conditional remedy would have left the Linux half unfixed while looking complete. The test is untouched — nothing weakened, nothing serialised. The classification is testable by injection so Windows raw error 33 is proven on Linux CI rather than waiting on a nightly.

And the reproduction attempt is RECORDED rather than omitted: "200 concurrent Linux stress runs at parallelism 16 (no reproduction)". That is exactly what I asked for — reproduce before fixing, or say so and record the attempt rather than declaring it fixed. Writing down a failed reproduction is the harder and more useful thing to do, and most PRs would have quietly dropped it.

ONE DISTINCTION MISSING, and it is the criterion I added when you found the Linux sighting. Two things shipped with different standing: the contention classification is ESTABLISHED — Windows returns raw 33, Rust does not map it to WouldBlock, verified — while the EINTR retry is NOT, because 200 runs did not reproduce the flake and nothing shows EINTR was ever the cause.

I do not object to the EINTR handling. Retrying an interrupted syscall is correct by standard regardless, so it fixes a real omission rather than guessing at this bug. But the summary reads as though both address the observed symptom, and they do not.

THE REQUEST I MADE ON THE PR is about how the spec closes. The Linux flake remains unexplained; neither shipped change is known to address it. If BUG-1303 completes silently it becomes a spec whose acceptance is met while its motivating symptom is unexplained — the same shape as BUG-1287 reading Completed with a fix that clears nothing, which we are still cleaning up. A paragraph saying the Windows defect is fixed and verified, the Linux sighting could not be reproduced in 200 attempts, and a recurrence is a new investigation rather than a regression, costs nothing and saves the next person from assuming it was solved.

Your Linux sighting is what made this spec correct, incidentally. My original framing was Windows-only and would have invited exactly the cfg-gated remedy this PR correctly avoids.
